Medical Drug Clinical Criteria
Subject: Atezolizumab (Tecentriq, Tecentriq Hybreza)
Document #: CC-0128 Publish Date: 07/28/2026
Status: Revised Last Review Date: 06/08/2026
Table of Contents
Overview Coding References
Clinical criteria Document history
Overview
This document addresses the use of Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab and
hyaluronidase-tqjs). Tecentriq is an anti-programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) monoclonal antibody primarily used to
treat non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and small cell lung cancer (SCLC).
The FDA approved indications for Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-
tqjs) includes:
• Individuals requiring first-line or maintenance therapy for metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC.
• Individuals requiring subsequent therapy of metastatic nonsquamous and squamous NSCLC.
• Individuals requiring first-line therapy as single agent for metastatic NSCLC.
• Individuals with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (SCLC).
• Individuals requiring first-line treatment of unresectable or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
• Individuals with unresectable or metastatic melanoma in combination with cobimetinib and vemurafenib with
BRAF V600 mutation positive disease.
• Individuals using as adjuvant treatment following resection and platinum-based chemotherapy for Stage II to
IIIA NSCLC whose tumors have PD-L1 expression on ≥ 1% of tumor cells.
• Individuals with alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS).
• In combination with Zepzelca (lurbinectedin) for the maintenance treatment of adults with extensive-stage
small cell lung cancer whose disease has not progressed after first-line induction therapy with Tecentriq or
Tecentriq Hybreza, carboplatin, and etoposide.
• As adjuvant treatment of adult patients with MIBC after cystectomy who have circulating tumor DNA
molecular residual disease (ctDNA MRD)
In 2016, Tecentriq received accelerated approval for the treatment of previously platinum-treated metastatic urothelial
carcinoma (mUC) based on results from Cohort 2 of the IMvigor210 study. Continued FDA approval was contingent
upon confirmatory results from the IMvigor211 trial, which did not meet its primary endpoint of overall survival in the
PD-L1–high population. The FDA subsequently designated IMvigor130 as the new post-marketing requirement,
which remains ongoing pending final analysis.
The National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) provides additional recommendations with a category 1 or 2A
level of evidence for the use of:
• Individuals with cervical cancer use in first-line, second-line, or subsequent therapy in combination and for
continued maintenance therapy.
• Individual with small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix as first-line, second-line, or subsequent
therapy in combination and continued as a single agent (or in combination with bevacizumab (or
bevacizumab biiosimilars)) for maintenance therapy.
• Individual is using for non-chemoimmunotherapy (Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor)-based regimen in
combination with venetoclax and obinutuzumab for Richter transformation in patients with CLL/SLL
• Individuals with stage III colon or rectal cancer with dMMr/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 mutation
• Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilars) for hepatocellular
carcinoma.
• Individual is using for cutaneous melanoma in combination with vemurafenib and cobimetinib for BRAF
V600 mutation.
1

• Individual is using for peritoneal mesothelioma as subsequent systemic therapy in combination with
bevacizumab if not previously treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors
• Individuals requiring first-line, subsequent, or maintenance therapy for recurrent or advanced squamous or
nonsquamous NSCLC.
• Individuals requiring subsequent therapy for recurrent or advanced nonsquamous and squamous NSCLC.
• Individual is using for small bowel in dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 tumor mutation with ultra-hypermutated
phenotype.
• Individuals with extensive stage small cell lung cancer (SCLC).
• Individual is using for alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS).
• Individual us using for thymic cancer in combination with carboplatin
NCCN has 2A recommendations to use Tecentriq Hybreza as a substitute for Tecentriq in all indications.
Definitions and Measures
Actionable molecular markers include EGFR, KRAS, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, NTRK1/2/3, MET, RET, ERBB2 (HER2)
and NRG1 mutations. The NCCN panel recommends testing prior to initiating therapy to help guide appropriate
treatment. If there is insufficient tissue to allow testing for all of these markers, repeat biopsy and/or plasma testing
should be done. If these are not feasible, treatment is guided by available results and, if unknown, these patients are
treated as though they do not have driver oncogenes (NCCN 1, 2A).
Adjuvant treatment: Additional cancer treatment given after the primary treatment to lower the risk that the cancer will
come back. Adjuvant therapy may include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy, or
biological therapy.
ECOG Performance Status: A scale used to determine the individual's level of functioning. This scale may also be
referred to as the WHO (World Health Organization) or Zubrod score which is based on the following scale:
• 0= Fully active, able to carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction
• 1= Restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or
sedentary nature, e.g., light housework, office work
• 2= Ambulatory and capable of all selfcare but unable to carry out any work activities. Up and about more
than 50% of waking hours
• 3= Capable of only limited selfcare, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours
• 4= Completely disabled. Cannot carry on any selfcare. Totally confined to bed or chair
• 5= Dead
Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer: Cancer has spread to other parts of the body and could include the fluid
around the lungs.
Immune checkpoint inhibitor: A type of drug that blocks certain proteins made by some types of immune system cells,
such as T cells, and some cancer cells. When these proteins are blocked, the “brakes” on the immune system are
released and T cells are able to kill cancer cells better. Examples of checkpoint proteins found on T cells or cancer
cells include programmed death (PD)-1, PD-ligand 1 (PD-L1), and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte–associated antigen
(CTLA)-4/B7-1/B7-2 (NCI, 2018).
Kinase inhibitor: Type of drug which works by blocking several enzymes that promote cell growth, which has been
found to be an effective approach to treat a variety of cancers.
Line of therapy:
• First-line therapy: The first or primary treatment for the diagnosis. This may include surgery, chemotherapy,
radiation therapy or a combination of these therapies.
• Second-line therapy: Treatment given when initial treatment (first-line therapy) is not effective or there is
disease progression.
• Third-line therapy: Treatment given when both initial (first-line therapy) and subsequent treatment (second-
line therapy) are not effective or there is disease progression.
Locally advanced cancer: Cancer that has spread from where it started to nearby tissue or lymph nodes.
Metastatic: The spread of cancer from one part of the body to another. A metastatic tumor contains cells that are like
those in the original (primary) tumor and have spread.
2

Neoadjuvant treatment: Treatment given as a first step to shrink a tumor before the main treatment, which is usually
surgery, is given. Examples of neoadjuvant therapy include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and hormone therapy. It
is a type of induction therapy.
Programmed death (PD)-1 proteins: PD-1 proteins are found on T-cells and attach to PD ligands (PD-L1) found on
normal (and cancer) cells (see immune checkpoint inhibitor above). Normally, this process keeps T-cells from
attacking other cells in the body. However, this can also prevent T-cells from attacking cancer cells in the body.
Examples of FDA approved anti-PD-1 agents include Keytruda (pembrolizumab), Opdivo (nivolumab), and Libtayo
(cemiplimab).
Programmed death ligand (PD-L)-1: The ligands found on normal (and cancer) cells to which the PD-1 proteins
attach (see immune checkpoint inhibitor above). Cancer cells can have large amounts of PD-L1 on their surface,
which helps them to avoid immune attacks. Examples of FDA approved anti-PD-L1 agents include Bavencio
(avelumab), Tecentriq (atezolizumab), and Imfinzi (durvalumab).
Clinical Criteria
When a drug is being reviewed for coverage under a member’s medical benefit plan or is otherwise subject to
clinical review (including prior authorization), the following criteria will be used to determine whether the drug
meets any applicable medical necessity requirements for the intended/prescribed purpose.
Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs)
Requests for Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs) may be
approved if the following criteria are met:
I. Individual is under 19 years of age;
OR
II. Individual has a diagnosis of one of the following:
A. Treatment of stage III colon cancer (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual has deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) or polymerase epsilon/delta
(POLE/POLD1) mutation with ultra-hypermutated phenotype [e.g., TMB > 50 mut/Mb]; AND
2. Individual is using in combination with FOLFOX or CAPEOX; AND
3. Using as adjuvant therapy;
OR
B. Advanced or metastatic colon cancer (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual has deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) or polymerase epsilon/delta
(POLE/POLD1) mutation with ultra-hypermutated phenotype [e.g., TMB > 50 mut/Mb]; AND
2. Individual is using as a single agent; AND
3. Individual has not had previous treatment with a checkpoint inhibitor;
OR
C. In non-chemoimmunotherapy-based regimen in combination with venetoclax and obinutuzumab for
Richter transformation in chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (NCCN 2A);
OR
D. First-line treatment of advanced, unresectable, or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) (Label,
NCCN 1, 2A); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilar);
OR
E. As subsequent-line systemic therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilar) for progression on
or after systemic therapy; AND
2. Individual has not had previous treatment with a checkpoint inhibitor;
OR
F. As subsequent-systemic therapy for peritoneal mesothelioma; AND
1. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilars); AND
2. Individual has not had previous treatment with a checkpoint inhibitor;
OR
3

G. First-line treatment of recurrent, advanced or metastatic nonsquamous non-small cell lung Cancer
(NSCLC) (Label, NCCN 2A); AND
1. Using in one of the following ways:
a. Individual is using in a combination regimen with nab-paclitaxel (paclitaxel, protein-bound)
and carboplatin; OR
b. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilars),
carboplatin, and paclitaxel, if no history of recent hemoptysis;
AND
2. Individual does not have presence of actionable molecular markers(except an individual may be
KRAS G12C mutation positive);
AND
3. Individual has an ECOG performance score of 0-2;
OR
H. As continuation maintenance therapy for recurrent, advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC
(NCCN 1, 2A); AND
1. Using in one of the following ways:
a. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilars); AND
b. Individual achieved a response or has stable disease following first-line therapy with
atezolizumab, carboplatin, paclitaxel, and bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilars);
OR
c. Individual is using as a single agent; AND
d. Individual achieved a response or has stable disease following first-line therapy with
atezolizumab, carboplatin, nab-paclitaxel (paclitaxel, protein-bound);
OR
I. In recurrent, advanced, or metastatic squamous NSCLC disease (NCCN 1); AND
1. Using in one of the following ways:
a. Individual is using as first-line therapy;
OR
b. Individual is using as maintenance therapy; AND
c. Individual achieved a response or has stable disease after first-line therapy with
atezolizumab;
AND
2. Individual is using as a single agent; AND
3. Individual has PD-L1 expression (≥50%); AND
4. Individual has tumors that are negative for actionable biomarkers (except KRAS G12C mutation
positive); AND
5. Individual has an ECOG performance status of 0-2;
OR
J. As monotherapy treatment for recurrent, advanced, or metastatic squamous NSCLC disease (NCCN
2A); AND
1. Individual has an ECOG status of 3; AND
2. Using as first line therapy, subsequent therapy, or continuation maintenance therapy in those who
achieve a response or stable disease after first-line therapy with atezolizumab or atezolizumab
hyaluronidase-tqjs;
OR
K. As subsequent systemic treatment for recurrent, advanced, or metastatic NSCLC ( NCCN 1, 2A); AND
1. Individual has no prior progression on a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor;
OR
L. Treatment of stage IB to IIIB resected NSCLC (NCCN 1); AND
1. Using in one of the following ways:
a. Individual received previous adjuvant therapy; AND
b. Individual has PD-L1 expression on tumor cells [TC] that is greater than or equal to 1% [TC ≥
1%]; AND
c. Individual has no known EGFR mutations or ALK gene fusions;
OR
d. As systemic therapy after completion of adjuvant chemoradiation;
OR
M. Treatment of unresectable or metastatic melanoma (Label); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with cobimetinib and vemurafenib; AND
2. Individual has BRAF V600 mutation positive disease;
4

OR
N. Treatment of advanced or metastatic rectal cancer (NCCN 2A); AND
O. Individual has dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 mutation with ultra-hypermutated phenotype (e.g., TMB >
50 mut/Mb) (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual has not had previous treatment with a checkpoint inhibitor;
2. Individual is using as a single agent;
OR
P. Adjuvant treatment of small bowel adenocarcinoma (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual has dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 mutation with ultra-hypermutated phenotype (e.g.,
TMB > 50 mut/Mb); AND
2. Individual is using in combination with FOLFOX or CAPEOX;
OR
Q. Treatment of advanced or metastatic small bowel adenocarcinoma (NCCN 2A): AND
1. Individual has dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 mutation with ultra-hypermutated phenotype (e.g.,
TMB > 50 mut/Mb); AND
2. Individual has not had previous treatment with a checkpoint inhibitor; AND
3. Individual is using as a single agent;
OR
R. First-line treatment of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) (Label, NCCN 1, 2A); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with etoposide and carboplatin (followed by maintenance
atezolizumab monotherapy); OR
2. Individual is using as primary maintenance therapy in combination with Zepzelca (lurbinectedin) with
stable disease after four cycles of carboplatin/etoposide + atezolizumab (or atezolizumab
hyaluronidase-tgis);
OR
S. Treatment of alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) (Label, NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual is using as monotherapy;
OR
T. As postoperative or first-line systemic therapy for thymic carcinoma (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel;
OR
U. Treatment of persistent, recurrent or metastatic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervical
cancer (NECC); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with etoposide and platinum-therapy (NCCN 2A); OR
2. Individual is using as a single agent maintenance therapy;
OR
V. Treatment of cervical cancer adenocarcinoma; AND
W. Individual is using in one of the following ways:
1. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab, paclitaxel, and cisplatin or carboplatin (NCCN
1); OR
2. If using as subsequent therapy, atezolizumab was not used previously as first-line; OR
3. If using as maintenance therapy, atezolizumab and bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilar) may
be continued;
OR
X. Treatment of mesothelioma including pericardial, tunica vaginalis, and testis (NCCN 2A); AND
1. Individual is using in combination with bevacizumab (or bevacizumab biosimilar); AND
2. Individual is using as subsequent therapy;
OR
Y. Treatment of muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) (Label); AND
1. Individual is using as a single agent for adjuvant treatment in those with MIBC after cystectomy who
have circulating tumor DNA molecular residual disease (ctDNA MRD).
Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs) may not be approved when
the above criteria are not met and for all other indications.
Step Therapy
5

Note: When Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab) is deemed approvable based on the clinical criteria above, the benefit
plan may have additional criteria requiring the use of a preferred1 agent or agents.
Tecentriq Hybreza (atezolizumab) Step Therapy
A list of the preferred products is available here:
Requests for Tecentriq Hybreza may be approved if the following criteria is met:
I. Individual is unable to use intravenous Tecentriq (atezolizumab) due to no venous access.
1Preferred, as used herein, refers to agents that were deemed to be clinically comparable to other agents in the same
class or disease category but are preferred based upon clinical evidence and cost effectiveness.

member.
